proved_results.statement: For the r51 low-disjoint three-hub normal form R=R_H[I,Z], G=ZZ^T, the complete rank-three spectral volume decomposes exactly into Pk=|detB| e_k(G), k=0..3, and detG/det(I+G)<2^-12 forces max(P0,P1,P2)>5P/16.
Low disjointness gives s3<1/15. If s2>0, one literal hub deletion has W_h>=s1s2/3>=e2/9 and true normal residual squared detG/W_h<=3s3<1/5; if s2=0 then rank Z<=1.
For actual hub pivot a=a0+d_h, the residual cross matrix is [(d_h/a)bq+C-bb^T/a]Z_J+(d_h/a)b n_h; only the second term is truly normal to the strong two-row tail plane.

scoped_density_implication: When the selected hub diagonal perturbation vanishes and core pivot a is nonzero, Delta_h=|detB|sqrt(W_h)/|a| and the completed scalar-pivot/rank-two-cross theorem gives ||p_Q||_inf <= 8[|a||detB|sqrt(W_h)]^-1/4.

partner_result_applied.application: After whitening the strong two-row tail frame, under max leverage<=1/2 the tangential shared leakage is removed exactly. At r=1/64, ||g_off||_inf<=256/|lambda_*|. The residual shared component is the true normal n_h with norm<1/sqrt(5). If the leverage gate fails, at most three literal tail coordinates have leverage>1/2.

corrections_consumed: bounded-density alone does not give law-uniform pointwise quadratic-phase van-der-Corput decay
unresolved_implication: Jointly consume max(P0,P1,P2)>5P/16 and the remaining true normal statistic without discarding the same-bank diagonal perturbation or taking a curved-fiber supremum.
next_step: QFORM-MIXED-LAYER-NORMAL-INNOVATION-RECEIVER-v1: build a product-weighted curved receiver for the normal term; on failure of the diffuse two-frame gate, route the at-most-three heavy tail coordinates to a finite physical-hub compiler.
